editorial:
Imagine yourself dropped right into the middle of the Sahara Desert, surrounded by giant rock walls and endless sand. That is exactly where you go in this beautiful story. You get to follow a group of Algerian and French climbers as they tackle the Hoggar Mountains. It is not just about the sport of climbing, though. You feel the bond between these people and the deep respect they have for the land. The movie also follows Thomas Dulac, who comes back to a spot he climbed a decade ago. With the soothing voice of singer Djam guiding you, the whole experience feels like a peaceful yet exciting journey into a part of the world that most people only see in postcards.

What really makes this work is the stunning look of the desert. The views are so big and bright that you will feel like you are actually there. The pacing is steady, giving you time to breathe and think, though some might find the slower parts a bit too long. If you love nature and stories about friendship, you need to see this. To get the full effect, you should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or rent it on Apple TV. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is a great move because the colors are just that good.
endingExplained: At the end, Thomas Dulac finally reaches the peak he first climbed years ago. This moment shows how much he has changed as a person over ten years. The film wraps up with a powerful message about how nature helps us find ourselves. You see the climbers sharing a final moment of brotherhood under the stars, proving that the journey and the friendships were more important than just reaching the top of the mountain.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves nature documentaries and stories about human connection.
